question: Should OpenClaw add `auth` as a conditional top-level public alias even though `openclaw models auth list` already provides the capability and plugins may own the same root?
rationale: A new public CLI root and permanent plugin-ownership exception are product and compatibility choices that cannot be inferred from green tests or implemented safely as routine contributor follow-up.

options.title: Keep the canonical models command
options.body: Decline the alias and close this PR, preserving one documented auth-list path and avoiding a conditional public command root.

options.title: Sponsor the conditional alias
options.body: Accept the new CLI direction, then require conditional-availability documentation and redacted live proof for both core fallback and plugin-owned `auth` behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep the canonical models command
recommendation.body: Decline the alias and close this PR, preserving one documented auth-list path and avoiding a conditional public command root.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the plugin root registration and overlap contract that this alias changes.
